question: An ant lifts 20 times its own weight. Scaled up 100 times in every direction, how many times its own weight could it lift?
move: Scale anything up and ask which parts grow as area and which as volume.
trap: Assuming the ant keeps its twenty-to-one ratio at any size.
hint: Strength grows with a muscle's cross-section; weight grows with its volume.
steps: Strength follows muscle cross-section: 100 × 100 = 10,000 times stronger.
reference: Schmidt-Nielsen, Scaling: Why Is Animal Size So Important?, Cambridge University Press, 1984
